title: Reports Allege Tennis Match Fixing, ATP Denies Claims

image.attribution: Razzle-dazzle at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Tennis players began to play at the Australian Open as two news organizations reported allegations of match-fixing based on leaked documents they received.

The BBC and Buzzfeed said that during the past decade the sport’s Tennis Integrity Unit (TIU) was repeatedly warned about the potential throwing of matches by 10 players ranked in the top 50, but none ever faced punishment.

Chris Kermode, the president of the Association of Tennis Professionals, said the TIU has not found any evidence to back up the allegations and does not rely on suspicion or hearsay.

“The Tennis Integrity Unit and the tennis authorities absolutely reject any suggestions that evidence of match-fixing has been suppressed for any reason or isn’t being thoroughly investigated,” Kermode said.

According to the BBC and Buzzfeed, eight of the suspected players were in this year’s Australian Open draw. The reports said a 2007 probe by the ATP found that betting rings in Russia and Italy made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting on matches that investigators believed to be fixed.

Novak Djokovic, the world’s top-ranked men’s tennis player, said that in 2007 people who worked with him were approached with a proposal for him to fix a match, which he did not.

Djokovic said there is no room for corruption in the sport, and that until there is evidence involving active players, then reports are only speculation.

“For me, that’s an act of unsportsmanship, a crime in sport, honestly. I don’t support it. I think there is no room for it in any sport, especially in tennis,” he said.

questions.question: What has the Tennis Integrity Unit been warned about in the past?
options: The potential for players to become overly competitive.
The possibility of match-fixing involving top-ranked players.
Increased scrutiny from media organizations over player conduct.
Insufficient funding for player development programs.
questions.answer: The possibility of match-fixing involving top-ranked players.

questions.question: What was the TIU’s reaction to the accusations?
options: They acknowledged the risks and promised an inquiry.
They launched an immediate investigation into all players.
They rejected the allegations and stated no evidence exists.
They expressed concern but did not initiate any actions.
questions.answer: They rejected the allegations and stated no evidence exists.

questions.question: How did betting rings in Russia and Italy make lots of money in the past?
options: By promoting legitimate gambling activities during tournaments.
Through organizing legal betting events without player knowledge.
By betting on matches that were believed to be fixed.
By encouraging players to increase their betting odds.
questions.answer: By betting on matches that were believed to be fixed.
